summary: The Ocean's Fever is an interactive Progressive Web App (PWA) that transforms NASA's Sea Surface Temperature (SST) visualizations into dynamic audio soundscapes. Addressing the Earth Information Jukebox challenge, we used computer vision (Python/OpenCV) to analyze video frames and map ocean heat to pitch and audio filters in real-time (Tone.js). As ocean temperatures rise (red), the sound becomes more intense and muffled, creating a multi-sensory experience. This makes complex climate data accessible to visually impaired users and engaging for the public, fulfilling NASA's mission of inclusive science communication.
details:
`Our project translates complex climate data into sound. We used Python and OpenCV to process NASA's Sea Surface Temperature video frame by frame, extracting the average color (heat) and generating a JSON dataset. The web app uses Tone.js to read this data in real-time. As the video shows hotter ocean currents (red), the audio pitch rises, and a low-pass filter muffles the sound to create a sense of urgency.

A major feature of our project is its accessibility. It is built as a Progressive Web App (PWA), meaning users can install it directly on their iOS or Android mobile devices without going through an App Store. Furthermore, screen readers and live text updates allow visually impaired users to "hear" climate change.

It also serves as an engaging educational tool. We developed it using Python, OpenCV, Tone.js, and the Web Audio API.`
